newsitem.title: USA: USDA says broiler exports trailing expectations.
newsitem.headline: USDA says broiler exports trailing expectations.

text.p: U.S. exports of broilers are running below expected levels this year, especially to Japan and Hong Kong, U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.

In its monthly world supply and demand report, USDA lowered its estimate of U.S. broiler exports this year to 4.58 billion lbs from last month's estimate of 4.84 billion lbs. In 1996, the U.S. exported 4.42 billion lbs of broilers.
Looking to 1998, USDA cut projected exports to 4.75 billion lbs from last month's estimate of 5.03 billion lbs.
"Broiler export prospects have weakened and exports, particularly those to Japan and Hong Kong, are trailing expected levels," USDA stated in the report.

However, USDA increased its estimate of 1997 U.S. exports of turkey to 535 million lbs from last month's estimate of 502 million lbs. For 1998, projected turkey exports were raised to 565 million lbs from the agency's previous estimate of 505 million lbs.
Last year, U.S. exporters sold 438 million pounds of turkey.
The stronger turkey exports are due mostly to increased sales to Hong Kong, the USDA said.
